questions.prompt: Which of the following is acceptable to include in a prompt to a general-purpose AI chatbot?
choices: The applicant's full name and last 4 of their SSN, since 4 digits alone aren't identifying
An image of the applicant's bank statement with the account number blacked out with a marker
'Applicant A's last 3 months of business bank statements show an average daily balance of approximately $40k, two NSF events, and consistent weekly inflows.'
The applicant's business name and the exact dollar amount of their requested loan
questions.explanation: Option C describes the underwriting-relevant facts using a generic placeholder and rounded figures — exactly what AI needs to be useful. The other three each leak identifying data: name+SSN-last-4 is identifying together, marker redaction on an image is rarely sufficient and the PDF metadata may still contain identifiers, and a business name plus an exact loan amount is a unique combination.

questions.prompt: An applicant sends you a paystub PDF. Underwriting needs to know whether income is stable. You want AI to help you draft a one-line summary for the file. What is the right way to proceed?
choices: Upload the PDF to the chatbot and ask 'is this income stable?'
Copy and paste the text of the paystub into the chatbot, then ask for a summary
Read the paystub yourself. Then prompt AI with: 'Applicant A's paystubs show gross pay of about $X biweekly, YTD roughly 9x that, single employer. Draft a one-line summary for the underwriting note.'
Forward the original PDF to underwriting and ask them to summarize it instead of using AI
questions.explanation: Option C is the placeholder pattern applied: you do the reading, you extract the underwriting-relevant facts, you anonymize them, then you use AI for the writing task. A and B both expose the full document including name, employer, and employee ID. D is correct that AI isn't strictly required, but it's a refusal to do the job AI is genuinely useful for; the goal of this path is to do this work efficiently and safely, not to avoid AI entirely.

questions.prompt: You're about to paste a prompt into ChatGPT and you scan it for the five-second check. The prompt mentions 'Applicant A,' avoids any SSN or account number, and uses rounded figures. But it also says 'this is for loan file LN-2025-04412 in our system.' Is that safe to send?
choices: Yes — the internal loan number is meaningless outside Kapitus and can't be used to identify anyone
Yes — only externally-recognizable identifiers like SSN matter; internal IDs are fine
No — Kapitus's internal loan numbers are identifying when combined with any other detail in the same prompt, and they tie the AI conversation log to a specific Kapitus record. Remove it.
Yes, but only if the chatbot has an enterprise data agreement with Kapitus
questions.explanation: Internal loan numbers feel innocuous because they're meaningless outside the company, but they're identifiers — they create a deterministic link between an external chatbot transcript and a specific Kapitus file. Combined with any other detail in the same conversation, they make the conversation traceable to one applicant. Strip them. The five-second check exists for exactly this case.
